findings.finding: Opens with the verdict and the cited source: "We did not replicate three of the four simulation headline findings of Chen (2021), who reported that mediation analysis in a sharp regression discontinuity design gives biased natural direct effects, percentile bootstrap confidence intervals that cover the true value far less often than the nominal level, and near-zero power for the mediated interaction", followed in the same sentence by all published-versus-ours numbers (0.00% vs 85.42%; 0.04 vs 43.62 points; 0.33 vs 47.07 points; 0.836 vs near zero). Verdict, source identity, original finding and evidence are combined as required.

The evidence limit comes next: "We could not establish why her results differ, as the step comparing her estimates with population values is unprinted and her result files are unavailable; her Head Start comparison is not established (no data)." Blocked RQ2 is not called a nonreplication.

The fourth headline keeps Chen's qualifier and its partial verdict: "Her tentative minimum n of 5,000 was partly replicated: 86.3% ... and 89.2% ..., but effects with both paths zero stay conservative."

"Her abstract puts Type I error and power within the robustness criteria, against her near-zero mediated-interaction power; 29 of the 46 statements we tested from her text agree." is compressed: a first-time reader is not told what the 46 statements are. Sentence 1 is about 110 words. Readable; listed as suggested fixes, not a failure.

Repeats the verdict first with exact counts ("in all 3,840 of 3,840 condition-cutoff cells (each of 1,280 simulated conditions analyzed at each of three cutoffs)") and quotes Chen's "All power for MINT is near zero" (printed p. 121), verified at source PDF p. 135.

Limit next (unprinted population-value step, unavailable result files; HSIS restricted-use data), then direction: "No headline effect reversed its sign ... about 140 times (imbalance) and over 1,000 times (shortfall) smaller". Ratios verified on unrounded values: 47.07/0.326 = 144, 43.62/0.0358 = 1,218.

Restates the tolerance (0.005, 0.005, 0.01 percentage points), calls it a rounding bound not a sampling band, and says magnitude labels are descriptive point-estimate comparisons, not equivalence tests.
The research questions come after the verdict (printed p. 7, verified at source PDF p. 21), and the paragraph maps H1-H4 and S1-S8 to sections.
Defines PNIE, TNIE, PNDE, TNDE, MINT, condition-cutoff cell and both-zero products on the page where they are first used; Section 3.1 (p. 3) defines them again in prose.
Defines 'Cell sets', 'Slack', 'If h = 0' and the trailing-digit cutoff notation; statement numbers are tied to the number column of statement_checks.csv.

evidence-packet.json is explained in words (machine-readable list of claims, locators, results, statuses, built by build_packet.py) rather than used as internal shorthand. No 'parent'/'executor'/'see the manifest' language anywhere; stage_checks.py cues returned no flagged phrases.

Body Section 4.1 (pp. 4-5) carries the same claim with Table 3.

H2 components (coverage 24.10-83.99%; truth above the CI) match Table 4.9 (source PDF p. 138) and Chen's p. 150 'systematically fell above the CIs'; p. 5 quotes her 'chief conclusion' (source p. 165, verbatim).

'near zero at every sample size; never reaches .80' matches printed p. 121 ('All power for MINT is near zero') and p. 148 ('never reached the .80 level'), verified at source PDF pp. 135 and 162; Figure 4.28 (PDF p. 136) shows the same near-zero lines.

findings.location: Table 1 row H4/E5; abstract last sentence
findings.finding: Chen's qualifier 'Tentatively' (source PDF p. 164) is kept as 'Tentative minimum n of 5,000' and 'her tentative minimum n'; p. 6 quotes the recommendation verbatim and p. 7 notes Chen calls it tentative and we read it literally.
Chen's headline conclusions are attributed to RQ3 with correct printed pages (147, 150, 121, 148, 150).

All 12 packet claims (H1-H4, S1-S8) appear with statuses matching the packet (not_replicated x4 incl. S1, partly x3, blocked S4/S6/S8, replicated S5, not_established S7). Every writer-manifest claim_map page/section locator was checked against the PDF (e.g. Table 7 statement 46 on p. 11, Section 10.2 on p. 16, Section 5.4 on p. 12) and is correct.

Every chapter (1-5), front matter, references and Appendices A-B is accounted for, matching the packet sections list; bias and coverage prose is stated as covered by the Table 4.8/4.9 comparisons, and the p. 148 summaries are named as not tested separately.

Read Chen's Type I and power sections (source PDF pp. 113-135) sentence by sentence: every result sentence is one of the 46 tested statements, one of the 7 excluded sentences (Table 8), a named source/restatement sentence (pp. 112, 114, 118, 121), or method/definition text. The p. 99 sentence 'The same pattern was observed for all three cutoff scores' is not named but is carried in statement 2's 'at all cutoffs' (suggested fix). Reran statement_checks.py: output is byte-identical to results/statement_checks.csv (sha256 73049ea9...). All 46 Table 7 rows match the CSV in number, page, statement text, cell-set counts and all three verdicts; counts reproduce (29/31 of 46; 13/14 of 18; 16/17 of 28; 15 robust disagreements; 39 under h = 0; 10 of 15 flip; 10, 11, 30, 41, 44 still disagree; 9 and 18 hold). Every 'statement N' reference in prose (9-11, 18, 25-29, 30-35, 39-46) matches the CSV number column.
The seven excluded sentences match the seven 'excluded' rows of statement_checks.csv with identical reasons and pages.

All seven packet limitations appear essentially verbatim and in order (R unavailable; unprinted aggregation/population values; HSIS unavailable; unreported SD-of-Y power analysis; cutoff-label inconsistency; correctly specified DGP vs Chen's functional-form explanation; h = 0 reading not tested against her runs).
Limitations 1-2 (cause unidentifiable) and 3 (HSIS) are stated on page 1, matching limitations_map entries.
Limitation 5 is developed with source locators (code p. 175-176, Chapter 4 p. 86, Table 4.8 note p. 88, Chapter 3 p. 55), all verified in the source.
Limitation 7 is stated where it applies with the qualifier 'readings of our own results, not tests of her runs, and they do not establish a cause'.

Separates Chen's model, estimators, design, code and published numbers from our re-implementation, run and comparison; E1-E3 published effects and Table 4.6-4.7 recomputations are labelled 'our calculation from her printed figures' (dagger in Table 9, p. 13; Table 1 caption).

Candidate causes are ranked with explicit statements 'untested, not established' and 'None is established'; the zero-estimate pattern is called 'a consistency observation, not a diagnosis' (p. 7). No cause of Chen's discrepancy is presented as established.

Claims about how the run was conducted (two computers, 401/879 conditions, versions, 13.7 core-hours, 1.1e-16 cross-host difference, R unavailable) are all supported by committed notes/run-record.md and simulation/fallback.json; validate_estimator.py was rerun and printed 1.07e-14 and PASS_ESTIMATOR_VALIDATION.

The post hoc choice of the H3 contrast cell is disclosed ('chosen after our full results were available'), matching the packet's multiplicity note; Table 5 gives every cell so the choice hides nothing.

Author Donna Chen, 2021 (December), title 'Statistical Mediation Analysis in Regression Discontinuity Design for Causal Inference', University of Nebraska(-Lincoln), advisers James A. Bovaird and Lorey A. Wheeler all match the title page and abstract page (source PDF pp. 1-2); Digital Commons URL matches the packet identifier.

"Type I error rate and power for all mediation effects were within or reached the robustness criteria, but bias and coverage were more often outside the robustness range" is verbatim at the cited abstract, PDF p. 3.

The stated original finding (biased direct effects, under-covering percentile bootstrap CIs, near-zero MINT power) and the tentative n = 5,000 recommendation faithfully state Chen's Chapter 4-5 headline conclusions.
Every quotation checked verbatim at its cited printed page (printed = PDF - 14): pp. 121, 147 (x3), 148 (x2), 150 (x2), 151, 87, 104, 58, 112 (x2), 118, 121, 54, 86; all found exactly.

Recomputed from Chen's printed Tables 4.8 (PDF p. 102) and 4.9 (PDF p. 138): E1 = mean(100 - within10) over six PNDE/TNDE rows = 85.4167 -> 85.42; E2 = 95 - mean coverage = 43.619 -> 43.62; E3 = mean(above - below) = 47.071 -> 47.07. From table49_ours.csv: E2 = 0.0358 -> 0.04, E3 = 0.3258 -> 0.33; E1 ours 0.00 from table48_ours.csv (all within). Signs, units (percentage points), magnitude 'smaller' and directions ('zero vs nonzero', 'same direction', 'same direction') are correct.

Tolerances 0.005, 0.005, 0.01 follow correctly from two-decimal printing (mean of rounded values within 0.005; difference of two means within 0.01) and are stated as rounding bounds; 'Descriptive point estimates; not equivalence.' is present and restricted to E1-E4.

'about 0.7 percentage points per cell for coverage and rejection (E2-E4)' is right for coverage near .95 but understates the per-cell SE of a rejection rate near .84 (about 1.2 points), and E4 is itself a 48-cell mean with far smaller error; no conclusion depends on it (suggested fix).
E4 = 0.836 reproduced from cells.csv (48 cells, mean reject 0.8361) and summary.json; Chen's missing numeric value is explained and no tolerance is invented.

Body text keeps the scalar comparisons honest: it repeats that no tolerance or magnitude label can be computed for E4 and that E5's magnitude is not established, while the claim verdicts rest on the qualitative conflict (H3) and the reported shares (H4).

Published 'PNDE and TNDE within [-.10, .10] in only 12.50-18.75% of conditions, with negative bias' is Table 4.8 plus printed p. 147; Ours 'within [-.05, .05] in 100% of conditions; largest |bias| 0.016' matches table48_ours.csv (PNDE/TNDE max 0.0155).

Published coverage range 24.10-83.99% and 'true value usually above the CI' match Table 4.9 (above-CI 14.08-75.55% vs below-CI 0.34-1.93%); Ours 'Coverage 94.6-95.6% ... misses on both sides at similar rates' matches table49_ours.csv (above 2.52-2.90%, below 1.84-2.71%).
Published cell matches pp. 121 and 148; Ours '0.836 at n = 500 for ah = .20; at least .97 for ah >= .13 from n = 1,000' matches summary.json (0.8361; minimum 0.9735 at n = 1,000, ah = .1326).

Published keeps 'Tentative'; Ours 86.3% / 89.2% and cutoff similarity (85.7-87.0%, 88.3-89.9%) match statement_checks.csv summary rows; 'both-zero products stay conservative' matches Type I about .002 for a = b = 0 cells. No cell is a placeholder and none is unsupported.

Justified: Chen states only 'near zero' (printed p. 121) with no printed value or precision, so no rounding tolerance exists and none was prespecified; the scalar contrast and our value 0.836 are retained, magnitude and direction are 'not established' because the published side is null, and the claim verdict 'no match' is kept separate. Polish: her Figure 4.28 (source PDF p. 136) plots MINT power near .05, so 'verbal result'/'gives no number' should say no numeric value is printed and the figure was not digitized.

Justified: the n = 5,000 recommendation is a qualitative statement over the whole grid; the applicability sentence explains why a pooled share would depend on the grid's effect-size mix. Packet component lists are empty, consistent with contracts: [] on H4. Verdict 'partial' is kept separate from the four 'not established' comparison cells, and the caption says the not-equivalence note applies to E1-E4 only.

items.independence_limits: I verified hashes, reran statement_checks.py, zero_estimate_check.py, table_arithmetic.py (byte-identical) and validate_estimator.py (PASS), recomputed E1-E3 and spot-checked over 25 body numbers against results files and source pages. I did not rerun the 13.7 core-hour simulation (cells.csv taken as given beyond spot checks against summaries), did not verify the cross-host check or ICPSR download first-hand, did not digitize Chen's figures, and did not verify non-Chen references against publishers. Writer-manifest isolation_note names earlier review files under older names (notes/editorial-review.json, notes/review-cold-pass.md) that do not exist on disk.

suggested_fixes: Abstract sentence 3 (p. 1): say what the 46 statements are (Chen's Type I error and power statements from Chapter 4) and separate the observation that her abstract conflicts with her near-zero MINT power from the 29-of-46 result.

Abstract sentence 2 (p. 1): the population-value step cannot explain H3 (rejection rates do not use population values, as p. 6 says); phrase the limit as 'her result files and aggregation code are unavailable' or name both reasons.
Table 1 E4 applicability text and p. 6 'Chen gives no number for the cell': note that her Figure 4.28 plots MINT power near zero but prints no numeric value, and the figure was not digitized.

Table 1 caption: give the Monte Carlo error for E4 correctly (per-cell SE about 1.2 points at a rejection rate near .84; E4 is a 48-cell mean) instead of 'about 0.7 percentage points per cell for ... rejection (E2-E4)'.
Table 1 typography: replace ASCII '>=', "c'" and hyphen-minus ranges with the body's typeset symbols and en dashes.
Section 5.2 (p. 8): name Chen's p. 99 sentence 'The same pattern was observed for all three cutoff scores' as carried in statement 2 (and the per-cutoff checks of statements 1 and 3).
Section 5.3/S4 (p. 11): mention Chen's RQ2 finding that RDD and RCT CIs gave different significance conclusions (abstract; printed p. 146), also blocked.
notes/availability.md: reconcile row 2 ('public-use data files are downloadable') with row 3 (V7 download contains no data files).
Section 3.3 (p. 4): the 1.1e-14 figure from validate_estimator.py is the maximum over both the scikit-learn and bootstrap comparisons; say so or report them separately.
